body:
[A755]

Closes #217

The ENTITY descriptor's `available_index` is "the same as the available_index field in ATDECC Discovery Protocol" (IEEE 1722.1-2021 Table 7-2, 6.2.2.15). ADP increments that field after each ENTITY_AVAILABLE it sends and resets it to zero when it sends ENTITY_DEPARTING. So READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) must carry the value of the last ENTITY_AVAILABLE sent: 0 after the first, N-1 after N, and 0 again after ENTITY_DEPARTING. Until now `E_RDESCENT` copied the AEM image's ENTITY descriptor whole, so the field always read the image's constant 0. milan-fpga's two-placement simulation found this (kebag-logic/milan-fpga#665, parent issue kebag-logic/milan-fpga#858).

## The fix

- `KL_adp_engine` gains `last_avail_index_o`. For each interface it holds the available_index the last ENTITY_AVAILABLE carried: the builder's own wire field, taken on the cycle the frame is handed to TX. It is 0 at reset and is cleared on the cycle an ENTITY_DEPARTING is handed to TX (6.2.2.15). The existing `aidx_r` holds the next frame's index, so it cannot stand in: it reads 1 after the first frame. Nothing on the wire reads the new register, so ADP's frames and timing are unchanged.
- `E_RDESCENT` (`hdl/aecp/ucode/gen_ucode.py`) now copies ENTITY bytes 0..35, builds the 4-byte index at octet 36, copies 40..309 and appends `current_configuration` as before. Its one `GATHER_EXT` (selector 0xE0) returns `adp_avail_index_i`. `KL_aecp_engine` routes that gather with `rdent_r`, which is set only where READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) is re-dispatched to `E_RDESCENT`, the same way START/STOP route the started bit's 0xD0.
- `protocol_processor_top` serves the index of the interface the AECP command came in on (`aecp_cmd_if_r`, the latch the registry port uses), because Milan v1.2 5.6.3 runs one advertise machine per interface. With one interface, or an out-of-range index, it serves interface 0's.

Unchanged: the top's ports, parameters and register map. Also unchanged: the AEM image (`hdl/aecp/desc`), every descriptor octet outside 36..39, everything under `hdl/srp`, and the MRP timers. The two new ports are on the internal engines only.

## Tests

- **pp_top section AI** (`make avail-index`) runs on a fresh processor. It does READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) before any ADPDU, after each of four ENTITY_AVAILABLE (each frame byte-exact, on ADP's own cadence), after ENTITY_DEPARTING (which carries 4), and after the re-enable (0, then 1). Each response is graded whole against the image's ENTITY descriptor with the expected index at octet 36, so every other octet is held to the image's.
- **pp_top IF4** (`make interfaces`, two interfaces) first runs interface 1's index ahead of interface 0's. It then reads the descriptor once on each interface, and each read must carry that interface's last index.
- **tb/adp_engine** P2, P3, P7 check `last_avail_index_o`: the frame's own index after each frame, 0 after DEPARTING, and 0 again after the restart advert while the next index is 1. In the two-interface build, IF4 checks it per interface and IF9 checks it after disable.
- The other pp_top sections that compare READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) with the image (A1, A10, N5b, M7, B4, B4b, B7, B11, K7, U7, G8) take octet 36 from the bench's own wire oracle. That is the index of the last ENTITY_AVAILABLE the bench captured, 0 after a captured ENTITY_DEPARTING or a reset. It is never read back from the processor.

Reproduction: section AI at the base `044cb25f` reads `AI: 16 checks, 4 failures`. The four failures are the reads after the second, third and fourth advertisements and after the second re-enabled one, for example `FAIL: AI2: READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) after that ENTITY_AVAILABLE carries available_index 1, the image's other octets byte-exact (got 354 B, available_index 0)`. At the head it reads `AI: 16 checks, 0 failures`.

| Arm | What it plants | Required failing check | Failures at the head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ai-entity-image-copy` | `E_RDESCENT` copies the image whole: the constant, the defect itself | `AI2: READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) after that ENTITY_AVAILABLE carries available_index 1` | 4 (AI2 at 1, 2, 3; AI4 at 1) |
| `ai-gather-constant` | the engine's gather answers 0: the constant again | the same | 4 |
| `last-index-is-next` | ADP serves the next frame's index | `P2 last ENTITY_AVAILABLE's available_index` | 5 |
| `last-index-is-next-top` | the same, at the processor | `AI2: ... carries available_index 0` | 6 |
| `last-index-kept-after-departing` | the last index survives an ENTITY_DEPARTING | `P7 last ENTITY_AVAILABLE's available_index 0 after DEPARTING` | 1 |
| `last-index-kept-after-departing-top` | the same, at the processor | `AI3: READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) after ENTITY_DEPARTING` | 1 |
| `if-top-aidx-interface-0` | the top serves interface 0's index to both interfaces | `IF4: READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) on each interface` | 1 |

The first two are in `tb/pp_top/aecp_dispatch_mutants.py` and the other five in `tb/adp_engine/mutants.py`. Each must fail its named check. The engine's two-interface IF4 and IF9 additions fail under `last-index-is-next` and `last-index-kept-after-departing`, with 1 of 11 checks each (a separate measurement; the campaign runs those arms on the default build).

Two existing arms had to be re-anchored, with the same lines removed and inserted: `rdc-base-no-overlay`, whose context now holds the `rdent_r` line, and `store-link-detector-resets-up`, whose context the new harness reset line moved. Both are KILLED at the head, and all 507 tracked patches apply there.

## Measured at the head `794f844`

On a clean clone, every gate that reads a changed file ended rc 0:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `make check`, `scripts/lint_hdl.sh`, `scripts/gen_matrix.py --check`, `git diff --check` | OK |
| `scripts/run_suites.sh` | 1,032,052 checks, 0 failing (36 suites) |
| `scripts/check-req-tags.py`, static and executed halves | 270 tags, 270 evidence lines in 14 suites, OK |
| `tb/pp_top/aecp_dispatch_mutants.py` | 108 of 108 |
| `tb/pp_top` `make aecp-mutants` | 67 of 67 |
| `tb/aecp_cmds` `make mutants` | 17 of 17 |
| `tb/adp_engine/mutants.py` | 68 of 68 (6 controls, 62 arms) |
| `tb/pp_top` `make ctr-mutants` | 18 of 18 |
| `tb/pp_top` ACMP, D3, GSI, notification and name-write campaigns | 103 of 103, 110 of 110, 30 of 30, 137 of 137, 1 of 1 killed |
| `tb/maap`, `tb/srp_top` `make mutants` | 32 of 32, 314 of 314 |
| `syn/yosys/run.sh`, `tb/elab_guards/guards.py --frontend yosys` | OK, 93 of 93 |

Consumer gate: a scratch milan-fpga at dev `ac0a01e3`, with this head pinned and its ROM digests re-recorded through `syn/yosys/ooc.sh --record-rom-digests`, committed locally and never pushed. Every rtl-fast job's commands ended rc 0: changes, verilator-lint, bdd-conformance, yosys-elaboration, publication-census, firmware-unit, the control, AECP and SRP firmware mutation campaigns, firmware-boundary and firmware-verilator. So did `tb/verilator/milan_dp`, and also `pp_shadow`, `nvm_cosim`, `milan_dp_mclk`, `capture_coherence` and `milan_dp_render`, which build the processor inside the datapath.

Two-placement simulation (kebag-logic/milan-fpga#665's `make -C tb/verilator/milan_dp twin`, run on a scratch copy with this head pinned): the owed row for this defect reports `owed row entity-available-index: the difference has gone, both halves send [READ_DESCRIPTOR to the first controller status 0 ...]`. The fabric's 195 frames are identical in time and bytes to the base's except one, the later READ_DESCRIPTOR(ENTITY) response, whose descriptor octets 36..39 read 1 instead of 0. The split's 260 frames are unchanged. Its other three findings, all from the all-fabric MVRP, are the same at base and head. By the twin's design a vanished owed row is itself a finding, so milan-fpga deletes the row when it takes this pin.

Area, base to head: sv2v of `hdl/` and the generated ROMs, then `synth_xilinx -family xc7 -flatten`, as `syn/yosys/run.sh` does, for the top at 2x2 and 8x8 streams and for the two engines alone:

| Run | LUT1-6 | FF | MUXF7/8 | RAM, CARRY4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol_processor_top` 2x2 | 42028 to 41954 | 20820 to 20853 | 353 to 406 | unchanged |
| `protocol_processor_top` 8x8 | 65192 to 65634 | 29891 to 29924 | 597 to 888 | unchanged |
| `KL_adp_engine` | 1470 to 1619 | 513 to 545 | 396 to 412 | unchanged |
| `KL_aecp_engine` | 10019 to 10256 | 4662 to 4663 | 2598 to 2693 | unchanged |

The 33 flip-flops are the 32-bit last index of the one interface plus `rdent_r`.
title: ENTITY descriptor available_index from ADP's current value (1722.1-2021 Table 7-2) (#217)
